correctness.rationale: For the exact 24 J37 vertices in Q(sqrt(2)), reconstructed all 2024 vertex triples with independent exact rational-pair field arithmetic, found precisely 26 supporting facets (8 triangles,18 quadrilaterals) and 48 distinct edges; independently reconstituted the Git tree from seven frozen blob SHA identities. The silhouette-edge criterion is sign(u·n_i) opposite sign(u·n_j), valid for generic orthographic projections. For p>0, 0<q<1 in the 16-symmetry fundamental wedge, checked no extra positive facet-event threshold lines beyond q, sqrt(2)q, (1−q)/sqrt(2), (1+q)/sqrt(2), 1−q, 1, 1+q, sqrt(2). Their five internal order-change values yield exactly 54 open chambers; independently checked every chamber sign count in exact Q(sqrt(2)), giving 20 N10,18 N11,16 N12 chambers. The A/B/C/D strip classification covers all generic directions, not merely finite samples, because no sign changes occur in a chamber. Independent spherical-Jacobian integration corroborated P10=0.44710927047909377, P11=0.4038628346745253, P12=0.14902789484638096 and sum 1; source exact spherical-triangle arctangent formulas make these exact constants, not floating estimates. Edge-angle classes 24 at pi/4 and 24 at arctan(1/sqrt(2)) independently reproduce mean 6+24 atan(1/sqrt(2))/pi. Exact symmetry reduction and elementary spherical-triangle area identity supply the global continuum proof; finite numeric hulls are ancillary. Boundary great circles are excluded by the theorem.

value.rationale: The 24-vertex elongated square gyrobicupola is an intrinsically natural Johnson solid, and its lookalike uniform rhombicuboctahedron has the same face sizes, vertex figure and exterior normal-angle multiplicities. The latter force an identical expected silhouette count, but the complete new J37 distribution has a positive eleven-sided shadow event absent from the uniform solid. The 54-chamber classification and exact Haar mass of each count are a natural, nontrivial geometric-combinatorial invariant; a future projection-geometry investigator can use the exact directional inequalities and probability law. This distinguishes global projection combinatorics from local metric/f-vector data; it is more than evaluating a known isolated table entry or a routine mean substitution.
